# Case Description

## Overview
Archived material describing a core conceptual model relied on
multiple incompatible implicit assumptions about system state
and operating conditions.

## Context
The material was used as a foundational reference, despite
never explicitly declaring its baseline assumptions.

## Inadmissibility rationale
The material requires mutually incompatible premises to hold
simultaneously. Making any single assumption explicit collapses
others, triggering epistemic instability.

## Boundaries
This case applies only to the core model description, not to
downstream implementations that explicitly re-specified assumptions.

# Case Description

## Overview
The archived material presents analysis that is internally coherent
and cautiously framed, but depends on contextual conditions that are
only partially specified and epistemically assumed.

## Context
At creation time, the surrounding environment and shared background
knowledge made the analysis interpretable and usable.
Over time, that context degraded without the assumptions being
re-specified.

## Inadmissibility rationale
The material fails epistemically because justification relies on
unstated premises, and contextually because those premises can no
longer be reconstructed or verified.

The case is classified as STOP to test multi-mode admissibility
without introducing new failure modes.

## Tension
If interpreted narrowly, the failure appears contextual.
If interpreted structurally, it collapses into epistemic failure.

This tension is intentional and used to test mode boundaries.

cases.case_text:
# Case Description

## Overview
The archived material is carefully written, cautious in tone,
and largely accurate. It would normally qualify for reuse.

## Context
The material was produced as guidance with explicit caveats,
and has been cited positively in several downstream contexts.

## Inadmissibility rationale
Despite surface rigor, the core justification relies on a
single unverified premise that cannot be independently validated.

Removing or weakening that premise collapses the argument.
Because the premise cannot be rehabilitated without external
assumptions, the material is classified as STOP.

## Boundary
This case is intentionally close to admissible.
It exists to test whether the system can enforce STOP
without escalating categories or relaxing standards.

cases.case_text:
# Case Description

## Overview
The archived material combines strong analytical reasoning with
implicit authority and situational urgency.

It does not fail cleanly along a single obvious dimension.

## Context
The material was produced in a high-pressure setting where rapid
decisions were required. Its authority derived from timing,
confidence, and partial expertise rather than formal mandate.

## Inadmissibility rationale
At first inspection, the case appears to require a new failure mode
to capture its structure.

On closer analysis, the failure resolves into:
- epistemic instability (confidence exceeds justification), and
- institutional failure (authority exercised without mandate).

No new failure mode is required.

## Test condition
This case exists to confirm that the taxonomy resists category creep
under pressure and ambiguity.

# Case Description

This file documents the context and content of the material
classified as inadmissible in the corresponding `gate.md`.

It exists to preserve traceability and rationale,
not to refine, correct, or rehabilitate the material.

---

## Overview

Brief description of the material being archived.

This may include:
- What the material is
- Where it originated
- When it was produced or used
- In what context it appeared

Avoid interpretation beyond what is necessary for identification.

---

## Source and provenance

Description of the source(s) of the material.

Include:
- Origin (system, project, individual, repository, etc.)
- Relevant timestamps or versions
- Links or references to `raw/` material where applicable

Do not reproduce large portions of the source material here.
Reference it instead.

---

## Context

Describe the operational, analytical, or historical context
in which the material was created or used.

This section may explain surrounding circumstances,
dependencies, or assumptions — but must remain factual.

---

## Inadmissibility rationale

Explain why the material is inadmissible,
in terms of the referenced failure modes.

This is a structural explanation, not a debate.
Do not propose fixes, alternatives, or mitigations.

---

## Boundaries

Clarify what this case does and does not cover.

This may include:
- Scope limitations
- Adjacent material explicitly not covered
- Known ambiguities or edge cases

---

## References

- Links to `raw/` material
- Related cases
- External references, if required for context

References are for traceability, not authority.

---

## Integrity

- This document is descriptive, not prescriptive.
- Once created, it must not be modified.
- Changes in interpretation require a new case elsewhere.

# Classification Gate

This file records the explicit classification decision
that the referenced material is inadmissible.

The decision captured here is final for this repository.

---

## Decision

**Status:** STOP

The material associated with this case is classified as inadmissible
for operational, analytical, or decision-making use.

---

## Failure Modes

This decision is based on the following structural failure modes:

- `<failure-mode-name>`

Failure modes must correspond to existing directories under
`/antecedents/failure-modes/`.

---

## Scope

This classification applies to the material as archived and referenced.
It does not imply claims about intent, authorship, or motivation.

---

## Notes

Optional clarifications, cross-references, or boundary notes
may be added here.

This section must not argue for rehabilitation, correction, or reuse.

---

## Integrity

- This file is authoritative for the classification decision.
- Once created, it must not be modified.
- Reinterpretation or reclassification must occur outside this repository.
